Yes — three call sites is exactly the threshold where a shared helper earns its keep, not a guess at a shape before there's evidence for one.

Before I'd sign off on the actual design, I'd want to see the three sites, because "same logic" can hide real differences that matter for what the helper's signature looks like:

- Same backoff curve (exponential, same base/cap) across all three, or did one drift because someone tuned it for a slower endpoint?
- Same definition of "retryable" — network errors only, or also certain 4xx/5xx codes? If one site retries on a condition the others don't, that's a parameter, not a reason to skip the helper.
- Any caller-specific state (metrics, logging tags) baked into the retry loop that'd need to come along, or is it purely mechanical (wait, retry, give up after N)?

If it's genuinely the same shape three times, this is a small, boring extraction — a function taking `fn, max_retries, base_delay` or similar, nothing fancier than that. I'd resist adding config for cases that don't exist yet (circuit breakers, jitter strategies, pluggable backoff algorithms) unless one of the three actual call sites needs it today.

Can you paste or point me at the three call sites? I'll ground the actual helper signature in what's really there instead of designing it off the label "retry with backoff."
